rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The bridge balances when P/Q = R/S and the galvanometer current is zero. On a metre wire the ratio is a length ratio, and a balance near the middle is the accurate one. Close the battery key before the galvanometer key.

rows.text: A ratio box of 1, 10, 100 extends the range.  ·  The galvanometer null does not depend on the battery voltage, but a larger voltage makes the null sharper until heating matters.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: This is the same bridge with the classroom names written out. P and Q may be the ratio arms of a box, while R is known and S is the unknown. Balance is still P/Q = R/S.  ·  When the ratio arms are the wire, P is proportional to the left length and Q to the right length. A jockey at the centre means the two gaps are equal if the wire is uniform.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: If the balance point is far toward one end, the percentage uncertainty in the short length is large. Changing the known resistor to bring the balance near 50 cm is good practice.  ·  The battery key is closed before the galvanometer key, and opened in the reverse order, so that a self-induced kick does not throw the galvanometer.  ·  The unknown can be a coil whose resistance changes with temperature. The bridge then measures that temperature effect, provided the wire itself stays cool.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: P/Q = R/S only at balance.  ·  The short length is the less trustworthy one.  ·  Closing the galvanometer first is the worse order.

rows.label: More ideas
